messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED — cross-region failover in progress. Automated traffic shift to us-west-2 triggered at 17:12 UTC. Some endpoints reporting high error rates and elevated latency in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. Paging current on-call.
Ben O'Connor: Oncall here, I'm seeing elevated 5xx rates from the frontend (~18% over baseline) and a spike in tail latencies. Is this the traffic-shift rollout?
Alice Nguyen: yes, we started the automated rollout for the DR exercise at 17:12. Initial checks passed, but dashboards show ~10-20% of traffic still routing to us-east-1. Health checks in that region show node readiness flapping.
Carol Park: Network team — I can run quick traceroutes from edge LB to backend pods in us-east-1. Suspect route propagation delay.
Dave Li: @Ben please paste the correlation id for a failing request so we can look logs & LB responses.
Ben O'Connor: sample request id: `req_20260315_171532_9f3b` — curl to the ingress returns HTTP 502 with backend_unavailable.
Erin (NetEng): running `traceroute -n 3.210.45.12` -> first hop shows next-hop inconsistent across probes, some paths go via a different AZ router.
Carol Park: AWS region control-plane reported a partial AZ egress stencil update; BGP updates were delayed for ~90s between us-east-1a and backbone routers. That could explain the half-open paths.
Alice Nguyen: Impact: customer-facing API returns 502/504 and prolonged token generation latency for sessions routed to the stale AZ. Estimated impacted percent: 12-18% global traffic. We should consider aborting the automated shift and perform a manual reroute with safe draining.
Ben O'Connor: Agreed. Oncall handoff: I'm taking lead. Alice, run the abort. Carol, coordinate with NetEng on forced route withdraw. Dave, prepare canary rollback for the autoscaler config.
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered — incident P-3 created, incident owner: Ben O'Connor.
PagerDuty: Paging Ben O'Connor (on-call) — acknowledged.
Alice Nguyen: Running abort: `redwood deploy traffic-shift abort --id shift-20260315-01 --reason "AZ route propagation lag causing unhealthy drain"`
Alice Nguyen: Abort command returned `OK` — controller reports rollback started, but we're seeing partial in-flight connections still reaching us-east-1 because of cached DNS and CDN edge affinities.
Carol Park: Asking cloud provider to withdraw stale routes from us-east-1a. @Erin can you request a BGP flush for the affected peering?
Erin (NetEng): Raised a ticket with cloud ops and issued `bgp session reset` on the egress router pair. Also reduced advertising for the affected AZ subnets. Waiting for propagation — cloud says ~2-3 minutes.
Dave Li: Logs from the LB show 502s tied to backend health check failures: `504 Gateway Timeout` when connecting to backend-container on 10.x.x.x:8080. Could be kube-proxy iptables stuck on nodes being partially drained.
Ben O'Connor: Let's stop draining nodes in us-east-1 temporarily to restore stable routing and allow LB to keep serving while route fixes propagate. Alice, can you cancel drains?
Alice Nguyen: Runbook step: `redwood node drain cancel --region us-east-1 --group app-prod` -> returned `canceled: 8 nodes`.
Carol Park: Cloud routing report now shows reduced BGP withdrawal lag. We're seeing full peering convergence on backbone.
Erin (NetEng): Confirming: traceroutes now consistent from multiple vantage points.
Ben O'Connor: Good. Monitor the 5xx rate and tail latency for 10 min. If we see recovery, we'll document postmortem and adjust traffic-shift playbook to include forced route verification pre-drain.
Alice Nguyen: Metrics: 5xx dropped from 18% -> 3% in 5 minutes after canceling drains and BGP reset. Latency tail (p99) trending down from 2.2s -> 600ms.
Carol Park: Noted unusual behavior: DNS TTL at some CDN edges was still honoring old routing for up to 30s leading to sticky sessions. We should add a pre-shift step to reduce TTL to 10s for affected records during future rollouts.
Dave Li: Also found kube-proxy kubelets in us-east had netfilter entries that delayed new conntracks — added a one-time script to flush conntrack on drained nodes:

# flush conntrack on nodes to avoid stale entries
for n in $(redwood node list --region us-east-1 --status drained); do
  ssh $n 'sudo conntrack -F'
done

Ben O'Connor: Thanks. I'm going to do a formal handoff to next shift in 30m and keep monitoring. Please annotate the incident with timelines and all commands run.
Alice Nguyen: Will document runbook deviations: abort -> cancel drains -> bgp reset -> conntrack flush. Noting customer impact: transient 5xx for ~16% traffic for ~12 minutes, no data loss, degraded latency for queued requests.
Carol Park: Filing follow-up action items: (1) add BGP propagation check to traffic-shift preflight, (2) TTL reduction automation before shifts, (3) add conntrack flush step or graceful wait window during drain.
Ben O'Connor: Agreed on the action items. Also recommend adding a synthetic probe that validates path symmetry after route updates (from edge -> backend).
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — automated controller reports rollback complete at 18:29 UTC. Postmortem required.
Ben O'Connor: Closing notes: customer impact communicated to support; CSMs notified for any high-touch customers. I'll start the postmortem doc and tag relevant owners. Great quick coordination — thanks all. :thumbsup:
